title: Targeting the cell adhesion related ligands MAC1 with Indirubin to inhibit AGE-RAGE signaling and mitigate colitis in an mouse model.
authors: Lin, Junchao; Wang, Chen; Yang, Gang; Liu, Yutong; Da, Yu; Zhou, Wei; Zhou, He; Wang, FaQi; Fan, Zhenzhen; Hou, Linqian; Wu, Tong; Wu, Kaichun; Liang, Jie
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究靛玉红通过靶向MAC1-CTCF抑制AGE-RAGE信号缓解结肠炎，涉及分子对接和双荧光素酶实验，但核心是炎症通路而非TF-DNA互作机制建模，方法深度有限。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, relapsing-remitting immune-mediated disorder, in which aberrant inflammatory activation within the intestinal submucosa is regarded as a central driver of its pathogenesis. Indirubin (IND), a bisindole compound extracted from Indigo naturalis and an active component of Qingbai Decoction (QBD), exerts anti-inflammatory effects. However, the specific mechanisms by which IND mitigates dysregulated mucosal inflammation in UC remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: The primary aim of the present study was to elucidate the anti-inflammatory properties and underlying mechanisms of IND using experimental models of UC. METHODS: Cellular and animal colitis models were established to evaluate the anti-inflammatory effects of IND. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we conducted proteomic sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, and immunofluorescence assays. Next, we assessed whether the anti-inflammatory effects of IND were dependent on macrophagy and the AGE-RAGE signaling pathway using specific pharmacological agonists and antagonists. Furthermore, the targeting and inhibitory effects of IND on the transcription factor Macrophage Antigen Recognition Receptor 1 (MAC1)-CCCTC-binding Factor (CTCF) were evaluated through molecular docking and dual-luciferase reporter assays. RESULTS: QBD exerted its anti-inflammatory effects in UC primarily by targeting the AGE-RAGE signaling pathway, with IND mediating this therapeutic action. Proteomic sequencing and mechanistic studies revealed that MAC1 and the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE), both critical components of the AGE-RAGE pathway activation, were significantly upregulated during UC progression and exacerbated inflammatory responses. Crucially, IND attenuated intestinal submucosal inflammation and reduced mucosal permeability in colitis models in a macrophage-dependent manner. In vitro experiments further showed that IND inhibited inflammatory responses specifically through the AGE-RAGE signaling pathway. Moreover, IND suppressed CTCF-mediated transcriptional activation of MAC1, thereby inhibiting downstream inflammatory cascades in vivo. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that IND targets MAC1 to suppress AGE-RAGE signaling, thereby alleviating UC progression.
abstract_zh: 引言：溃疡性结肠炎（ulcerative colitis, UC）是一种慢性、复发-缓解型免疫介导性疾病，其中肠道黏膜下层内的异常炎症激活被视为其发病机制的核心驱动因素。靛玉红（indirubin, IND）是一种从青黛中提取的双吲哚化合物，也是清白汤（Qingbai Decoction, QBD）的活性成分，具有抗炎作用。然而，IND缓解UC中失调的黏膜炎症的具体机制仍不清楚。目的：本研究的主要目标是利用UC实验模型阐明IND的抗炎特性及其潜在机制。方法：建立细胞和动物结肠炎模型以评估IND的抗炎效果。为探究潜在机制，我们进行了蛋白质组学测序、单细胞RNA测序和免疫荧光检测。随后，我们使用特异性药理激动剂和拮抗剂评估IND的抗炎作用是否依赖于巨噬细胞和AGE-RAGE信号通路。此外，通过分子对接和双荧光素酶报告基因实验评估了IND对转录因子巨噬细胞抗原识别受体1（MAC1）-CCCTC结合因子（CTCF）的靶向和抑制作用。结果：QBD主要通过靶向AGE-RAGE信号通路发挥其在UC中的抗炎作用，而IND介导了这一治疗效应。蛋白质组学测序和机制研究表明，MAC1和晚期糖基化终末产物受体（RAGE）——两者均为AGE-RAGE通路激活的关键组分——在UC进展过程中显著上调，并加剧炎症反应。关键的是，IND以巨噬细胞依赖性方式减轻了结肠炎模型中的肠道黏膜下层炎症并降低了黏膜通透性。体外实验进一步表明，IND通过AGE-RAGE信号通路特异性抑制炎症反应。此外，IND抑制了CTCF介导的MAC1转录激活，从而在体内抑制下游炎症级联反应。结论：总体而言，这些发现表明IND靶向MAC1以抑制AGE-RAGE信号通路，从而缓解UC进展。
